images.caption: Yevpatoria RT-70 radio telescope. Inside an antenna mirror of the radio telescope RT-70. There is a cabin “C” in the center of the main mirror, inside of it on the 1st and 2d floors there are racks of amplifiers on TWT and at the end there are amplifiers on the klystrons which radio broadcast the device “Goliaf”. On the third and fourth floors there are high sensitive cryogenic receiving complexes of 92, 18, 13, 6, 3.5, 1.35cm ranges. There is a counterreflector with four holds above the cabin “C” (the second mirror). The great mirror and the counterreflector are forming double-mirror system of Gregorian and Cassegrain.

images.caption: International experiment VLBI of radiolocation the space rubbish. The work was made as a scientific research “Interferometr” by Institute of radio astronomy NAS of Ukraine.The tasks of experiment:- checking the possibilities of multipoint radar complex after long pause in work and checking the modernization of radio telescopes;- exploring the objects of space rubbish in a method of VLBI-location with the aim to measure the changing of Dopler frequency and delaying for rectification the orbit options;- receiving reflected signals in radiometric made for the determination the period of rotation and object sizes;- training the technology of preparing and issuance targeting on radio telescope RT-70 for preparing to modernization of managing computable complex.
images.alt: International experiment VLBI of radiolocation the space rubbish. images.caption: Cover of the Soviet Union sent from Smolensk to Moscow on 15 February 1992, the day when the Union of Philatelists of Russia was organized. Stamped envelope with an imprinted definitive stamp of the Soviet Union was used and cancelled with a special postmark dedicated to this event. The letter was also franked with three more definitive stamps of the Soviet Union.

images.filename: Vitino, RT-70 radio telescope (planetary radar), Crimea.jpg
images.caption: Evpatoria RT-70 radio telescope (planetary radar) in Crimea is extraterrestrial civilizations ready. The antenna is a powerful planetary transmitter with diameter of 70m and operating range of 5-300 GHz. The telescope participated in almost all of Soviet space programs since 1978 for the exploration of deep space: Venera, Salyut, Vega, Astron, Phobos, Granat, Fobos-Grunt, Spektr-R and more. Evpatoria Center for Deep Space Communications and Exploration. Vitino, Crimea.

images.filename: Vitino, RT-70 radio telescope (planetary radar, space exploration radar), Crimea.jpg
images.caption: Evpatoria RT-70 radio telescope (planetary radar, deep space exploration radar) in Crimea is extraterrestrial civilizations ready. The antenna is a powerful planetary transmitter with diameter of 70m and operating range of 5-300 GHz. The telescope participated in almost all of Soviet space programs since 1978 for the exploration of deep space: Venera, Salyut, Vega, Astron, Phobos, Granat, Fobos-Grunt, Spektr-R and more. This telescope has also been used as a radar telescope in observations of space debris and asteroids, and to transmit messages to extraterrestrial civilizations. Up to 100 transmit sessions have been performed to various star destinations in Cygnus, Sagitta, Cassiopeia, Orion, Andromeda, Ursa, Major, Delphinus, Gemini, Virgo, Hydra constellations, with a beam signal power of up to 150 kW at 5 GHz frequency-shift keying. They are all expected to arrive at their destinations in 10 to 50 years. Evpatoria Center for Deep Space Communications and Exploration. Vitino, Crimea.
images.alt: Evpatoria RT-70 radio telescope (planetary radar, deep space exploration radar) in Crimea is extraterrestrial civilizations ready. This telescope has also been used as a radar telescope in observations of space debris and asteroids, and to transmit messages to extraterrestrial civilizations. Up to 100 transmit sessions have been performed to various star destinations in Cygnus, Sagitta, Cassiopeia, Orion, Andromeda, Ursa, Major, Delphinus, Gemini, Virgo, Hydra constellations, with a beam signal power of up to 150 kW at 5 GHz frequency-shift keying. They are all expected to arrive at their destinations in 10 to 50 years. Evpatoria Center for Deep Space Communications and Exploration. Vitino, Crimea.
